architecture.name: mla-qkv-dim-divergence
architecture.head_dims: The (qk_dim, v_dim) tuple space of modern latent/partial-RoPE attention: DeepSeek MLA absorbed cache tuple (576, 512) where 576 = 512 kv_lora_rank (latent, no-RoPE) + 64 qk_rope_head_dim; unabsorbed prefill tuple (192, 128) where 192 = 128 qk_nope + 64 rope and v_head_dim = 128; GLM-5/5.2 tuple (256, 256) with 256 = 192 qk_nope + 64 rope and kv_lora_rank 512; Qwen3.5 full-attention tuple (256, 256) with a 64-dim RoPE sub-slice (partial_rotary_factor 0.25); Kimi Linear MLA tuple (192, 128) with kv_lora_rank 512; llama.cpp additionally covers (320, 256) (Mistral Small 4) and (192, 128) (MiMo-V2.5) as first-class template cases.
architecture.qkv_dim_divergence: Yes - this is the defining trait of the MLA family, in two distinct senses. (1) qk_dim != v_dim at the KV-cache level: in weight-absorbed MLA decode, K per token is the 576-dim [c_KV(512) | k_rope(64)] latent vector while V is the 512-dim c_KV latent, so the attention kernel consumes genuinely asymmetric K and V head dims; DeepSeek's FlashMLA hard-asserts head_dim==576 && head_dim_v==512 (flash_mla_interface.py: 'head_dim should be 576 while head_dim_v should be 512'), and FlashMLA's README footnote [2] formalizes the two modes: 'MQA' mode = head_dim_k 576 / head_dim_v 512, 'MHA' mode = head_dim_k 192 / head_dim_v 128. (2) Even where qk_dim == v_dim (GLM-5 256/256, Qwen3.5 256/256), the head is internally a tuple: a no-RoPE body plus a small rope_dim (64) slice, so kernels need a (D, DV, rope_dim) description rather than a scalar D. Kernel-design consequence proven by llama.cpp: fattn-mma takes DKQ and DV as INDEPENDENT template parameters (template<int DKQ, int DV, int ncols1, int ncols2, ...>), with per-arch config tables keyed on the (DKQ, DV, ncols) triple and runtime dispatch asserting V->ne[0] per K->ne[0] case - head_dim as a tuple, not a scalar. MLA additionally enables a K==V data-reuse path: fattn-mma's V_is_K_view template flag exploits 'For MLA K and V have the same data. Therefore, iterate over K in reverse and later re-use the data', which halves smem tile pressure for the absorbed 576/512 shape.
architecture.kv_heads_gqa: MLA collapses KV to a single shared latent per layer, so absorbed decode is MQA-shaped: DeepSeek-V2/V3/R1 and Kimi-K2/K2.5 use num_key_value_heads effectively 1 in MQA mode (FlashMLA dense decode 'MLA Mode: MQA', 128 query heads at GQA ratio 128:1 over the 576-dim latent); GLM-5.2: 64 attention heads, num_key_value_heads 64 over one shared 512+64 latent (per-layer MQA semantics); Kimi Linear MLA layers: 32 heads / num_key_value_heads 32 (MQA-style, kv_lora_rank 512, q_lora_rank null). Qwen3.5 is ordinary GQA, but extreme: 32 Q heads to 2 KV heads (16:1) at head_dim 256. llama.cpp fattn-mma keys its GQA handling on ncols2 (KV rows per CTA: 1/2/4/8/16/32) and the 576/512 dispatch requires gqa_opt_applies (gqa_ratio>=2, plain mask, 16B-aligned strides), with model-specific narrowings: DeepSeek requires ncols2 in (4,16,32), Mistral Small 4 (320/256) is ncols2==32-only, MiMo-V2.5 (192/128) requires gqa_ratio%8==0 or %16==0, and llama.cpp's source notes a 'GLM 4.7 Flash' variant with gqa_ratio 20 at 576/512.
architecture.hybrid_pattern: The tuple shapes arrive inside per-layer hybrid stacks. Kimi Linear (KimiLinearForCausalLM, config verified): 27 layers = 20 Kimi Delta Attention linear layers (head_dim 128, 32 heads, per-channel fine-grained gating, short_conv_kernel_size 4) interleaved with 7 global MLA layers at every 4th layer (full_attn_layers [4,8,12,16,20,24,27], ~3:1); Kimi K3 (2.8T params) scales the same pattern to 69 KDA + 24 MLA layers. GLM-5.2's indexer config carries its own layer pattern: indexer_types alternate 'full' (every 4th layer, 3 of the first 4 then periodic) vs 'shared' (indexer states shared with neighbouring layers), index_topk_freq 4. Qwen3-Next (origin of the Qwen3.5 shape) uses 3:1 Gated DeltaNet : full-attention; Qwen3.5-397B-A17B's text config contains linear_attention layers (per SGLang issue #29577) plus full-attention layers at head_dim 256 / rope 64 / 2 KV heads. DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 add DSA sparse top-k (index_topk 2048) on top of MLA, which llama.cpp implements as a use_sparse gather template branch of fattn-mma plus a separate lightning-indexer kernel.
architecture.heterogeneous_dims: Yes - heterogeneous head geometry both across model families and within a single serving fleet: one cluster serves DeepSeek-V3 (576/512 cache, 192/128 prefill), Kimi-K2 (identical 576/512), GLM-4.5/GLM-5 (256/256 heads over 512 latent + DSA indexer head 128 x 32 heads), Qwen3.5 (256/256 with 64 rope, GQA 16:1), Kimi Linear (192/128 MLA on 7 of 27 layers, KDA 128 on the rest) - and llama.cpp even documents intra-ecosystem stragglers MiMo-V2.5 (192/128) and Mistral Small 4 (320/256). Within one Kimi Linear forward pass the head-dim workload literally alternates per layer between linear-attention 128-dim state updates and 576/512 MLA attention, which is why every major serving stack grew per-layer backend dispatch rather than a single kernel path. Within llama.cpp a single fattn binary carries symmetric instances (64..256, 512) plus exactly three asymmetric tuples (192,128), (320,256), (576,512), selected at runtime per op.

kernel_support.supported_dims: FlashMLA: fixed (576, 512) MQA-absorbed BF16 decode (SM90) plus FP8 sparse decode/prefill (SM90 & SM100); assert-gated, no template range. FlashAttention: scalar-template family up to 256; MLA added 2025-04 in the hopper/ FA3 branch only as a bespoke mma decode path taking q hdim 64 (q_rope), qv 512 (q_nope), k 64, v 512 (latent) per tridao in issue #1471 - not the generic 576 template the requester tried to compile ('I tried to patch the configs to compile a 576 version but it crashed'). FlashInfer: MLA present but arch-stratified - SM80 tensor-core MLA path is a legacy path (issue #3170 audit: 'device_arch == 80 ... SM80-only legacy path; use XQA MLA instead'), XQA MLA on SM90, trtllm-gen MLA on SM100, sparse-MLA variants for SM120; nothing for SM75. llama.cpp is the existence proof for tuple-space coverage on a template kernel: generate_cu_files.py sets HEAD_SIZES_KQ = [40, 64, 72, 80, 96, 112, 128, 192, 256, 320, 512, 576] with HEAD_SIZES_V_OVERRIDE = {576: 512, 320: 256, 192: 128}, auto-generating fattn-tile instance files (fattn-tile-instance-dkq576-dv512.cu, dkq320-dv256.cu, dkq192-dv128.cu) and fattn-mma DECL_FATTN_MMA_F16_CASE(DKQ, DV, ncols1, ncols2) instances; fattn-mma then applies per-arch config tables (Ampere/Turing/Volta/RDNA/CDNA) with nbatch_K2/nbatch_V2 chunk sizes, nstages, and Q_in_reg tuned per (DKQ, DV, ncols). Achieved via template instantiation per explicit tuple, NOT padding or generic autotune.
kernel_support.capability_gate: FlashMLA: SM90/SM100 floor (README Requirements: 'SM90 / SM100'); dense BF16 decode is SM90-only - gated on Hopper wgmma/TMA in the CUTLASS SM90 kernels, not on a missing feature Turing lacks in principle. FlashAttention MLA: Hopper-only (tridao, 2025-04-27, asked 'does it support A100?': 'No') - the FA3 hopper branch depends on wgmma; FA2 mainline never got 576. FlashInfer: overall builds for SM75-SM121, but its MLA paths gate at SM80 (legacy tensor-core MLA, being deprecated in favour of SM90 XQA MLA and SM100 trtllm-gen) - SM75 has no MLA entry at all. llama.cpp fattn-mma floor is exactly Turing (sm_75): dispatch is 'if (turing_mma_available(cc) ... ) return BEST_FATTN_KERNEL_MMA_F16', with a separate Volta path (mma m8n8k4 without cp.async), proving the real Turing blocker list is: no cp.async (nstages_target forced to 1/0, synchronous 16B memcpy loads), Turing mma m16n8k16 fragment layout requiring different softmax reduction code ('Turing + Volta: const int KQ_idx = l % 2', shuffle offsets first=2 last=1 vs Ampere), and 64KB smem requiring Q_in_reg=false plus K/V tile reuse at (576,512). Sparse DSA gather in fattn-mma additionally requires NVIDIA + turing_mma_available and non-HIP/MUSA.
kernel_support.fallback_semantics: Three distinct behaviours. (1) Hard error/assert: FlashMLA raises the 576/512 assertion in flash_mla_interface.py before launch; llama.cpp GGML_ASSERTs V->ne[0] per K->ne[0] case and GGML_ABORT('Unsupported head size') in fatnn-tile's default; vLLM logs backend rejection chains (e.g. FLASHMLA sparse 'only supported on Hopper and Blackwell devices') and falls through its backend preference list to TRITON_MLA on non-Hopper. (2) Kernel-family fallback inside one backend: llama.cpp picks BEST_FATTN_KERNEL in {VEC, MMA_F16, TILE, NONE}; asymmetric tuples have no VEC instances ('192 satisfies % 64 == 0 but has no vec instance (DKQ != DV); force it onto the MMA path') and fall to TILE on non-tensor-core hardware; unsupported combos return BEST_FATTN_KERNEL_NONE and the graph falls back to slower generic ops. (3) Full-stack per-layer fallback: vLLM/SGLang hybrid models route linear-attention layers to FLA/FlashKDA Triton kernels and MLA layers to whichever MLA backend passed the arch gate, so an unsupported (qk, v) tuple degrades per layer type rather than killing the whole model.
kernel_support.ci_hardware_coverage: FlashMLA: developed against H800 (SM90) - perf claims (up to 660 TFlops dense, 410 TFlops sparse decode) are Hopper-measured; no Turing/Ampere CI (and no such kernels to run). FlashAttention MLA: hopper-branch benchmarks only; issue #1471 confirms A100 excluded. FlashInfer: broad arch matrix claimed (SM75 listed as supported for the library generally) but its SM121 audit (issue #3170) shows per-path MLA availability tables maintained by hand, with the SM80 MLA path already marked legacy/unavailable - evidence that 'supported' claims rot per kernel, not per library. llama.cpp is the counter-example: fattn-mma's Turing config table is a maintained code path with Turing-specific correctness branches (KQ_idx fragment indexing) and its PR stream explicitly added 576/512 for DeepSeek, 320/256 for Mistral Small 4, 192/128 for MiMo-V2.5; whether any CI machine actually exercises Turing with those instances is not visible in the repo (GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS compile-time flag suggests most builds trim instances) - [uncertain]. vLLM: backend rejection logs from users on H100/H200 (GPUStack guide, HF discussion) show the fallback chain is exercised in the field, but vLLM V1 effectively requires SM80+, so sm_75 MLA coverage in production stacks is zero outside llama.cpp.

performance.turing_baseline: No published measured numbers for 576/512 (or 320/256) attention on Turing hardware were found; [uncertain] this row's conclusion is qualitative. Existence proof: llama.cpp fattn-mma ships a dedicated ggml_cuda_fattn_mma_get_config_turing table with explicit (576,512) entries - e.g. ncols 8/16: nthreads 64, occupancy 4, nbatch_fa 32, nbatch_K2 96, nbatch_V2 64, nbatch_combine 128, nstages 1, Q_in_reg false - and the master-branch dispatch prefers MMA_F16 on Turing whenever turing_mma_available, so DeepSeek/Kimi-K2 MLA decode runs end-to-end on T4/RTX 2080Ti-class GPUs today via llama.cpp (widely reported in r/LocalLLaMA deployments of DeepSeek-R1 distills and Kimi-K2 quants). For contrast, the same shapes on supported hardware: FlashMLA dense BF16 decode reaches 660 TFlops on H800 (~3000 GB/s memory-bound decoding claimed at launch); vLLM issue #35807 reports FlashInfer MLA beating FlashMLA >3x in some FP8 prefill/decode configs on Hopper-class GPUs. A Turing T4 (320 GB/s, 64KB smem/SM) running the same 576/512 tuple is memory-bound on the 576-dim K read; expect a small fraction of H800 throughput, but the shape itself is not the blocker - the config table proves occupancy-4 fits.
performance.d256_feasibility: In this item's context d=256 is the EASY member of the tuple space: llama.cpp instantiates (256,256) on Turing with Q_in_reg TRUE (config row: ncols 8, nthreads 128, occupancy 2, nbatch_fa 64, nbatch_K2/V2 128, nstages 2), i.e. the whole 256-dim Q and K pipelines hold in registers/smem on a 64KB-smem sm_75 part without chunking; the Turing smem budget for (256,256) is roughly nbatch_fa 64 x 256 dims x 2B = 32KB per tile plus Q, comfortably under the 64KB cap, and Volta (even older, 96KB smem but no cp.async) is also served. By extension the harder asymmetric tuples are handled by K-chunking only: (576,512) switches to Q_in_reg=false, nbatch_K2 96 (i.e. 192 dims of 576 per pass, 3 chunk iterations), nbatch_V2 64, nstages 1. For the sm_75 bridge this means a native d=256 template (ROUTE A) is consistent with what llama.cpp already runs on Turing, and adding the rope-split tuples (256,256,rope 64) for GLM-5/Qwen3.5 needs no new machinery - just a K-tile layout where the 64 rope dims ride the same chunked loop.
performance.cost_analysis: Concrete costs extracted from llama.cpp's tables (the only open template kernel publishing per-arch, per-tuple budgets). First, smem: on Turing, (576,512) uses nbatch_fa 32 K-rows; with V_is_K_view (MLA K==V) ONE tile serves both operands - 32 x 576 x 2B = 36KB worst case, fit under 64KB because nstages=0 on Turing (no cp.async double-buffering); on Ampere the same tuple uses nbatch_K2 288/nbatch_V2 256 with nstages 1-2, trading more smem for pipelining. Second, registers: Q_in_reg=false at (320,256) and (576,512) means Q streams from smem per K-chunk (extra ldmatrix traffic: DKQ/2 / T_A_KQ::J reloads per chunk), while VKQ accumulators (DV=512 across 64 threads = 16 half2 each) dominate pressure; nbatch_combine caps the final reduction width. Third, compute shape: absorbed MLA decode is MQA with 128 Q rows per KV row, so the mma count is dominated by the KQ^T product over 576 dims chunked in 96-dim nbatch_K2 steps (six chunk iterations) plus PV over 512 dims. Finally, compile time: each tuple multiplies instances by ncols sets - generate_cu_files.py notes ncols2 filtering to avoid compiling unnecessary kernels ('For Deepseek, go straight to the ncols1 switch to avoid compiling unnecessary kernels'; 576 only builds ncols2 in (4,16,32)), and GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS exists as an opt-out; this is the template-instantiation tax an sm_75 bridge would pay for covering even 3 asymmetric tuples across 2 arch tables.

design_fit.route: ROUTE B primarily (k-chunked asymmetric (qk, v) support on the existing 128-pipeline) with ROUTE C as the completeness play: the evidence uniformly shows that qk!=v and rope-split heads are handled in production kernels by chunking the K/D axis independently of the V axis while keeping separate template parameters for K and V dims - never by padding to a common scalar head_dim. ROUTE A (native d=256 monolith) covers the GLM-5/Qwen3.5 256/256-with-rope-64 shape but cannot express 576/512.
design_fit.recommendation: Treat head_dim as the tuple (DKQ, DV, rope_dim) in the sm_75 bridge's dispatch interface, mirroring llama.cpp: separate K and V template parameters plus a per-arch config struct (nthreads, occupancy, nbatch_fa, nbatch_K2, nbatch_V2, nbatch_combine, nstages, Q_in_reg) so each (tuple, ncols) gets a tuned case rather than a generic autotune. Minimum viable Turing tuple set for model coverage: (128,128) Llama-class, (256,256) + rope-64 split for GLM-5/5.2 and Qwen3.5, (192,128) for Kimi-Linear/DeepSeek prefill-style and MiMo, (576,512) with V_is_K_view tile reuse for DeepSeek/Kimi-K2 absorbed decode, and optionally (320,256) for Mistral Small 4. Next actions: (1) port llama.cpp's Turing config table values as the starting tuning grid for the bridge kernel's chunked-K loop; (2) implement the rope split as a dim-offset inside the K chunk loop (first 512 dims un-rotated, last 64 rotated) exactly as MLA's [latent | rope] layout requires; (3) skip FlashInfer/FlashMLA for sm_75 entirely - their MLA paths gate at SM80/SM90, so the bridge is the only viable CUDA-core-class vendor for these shapes; (4) before writing kernels, verify against llama.cpp's fattn-mma reference outputs at all five tuples since it is the only existing sm_75-capable implementation.
design_fit.numerics_risks: Documented in-source: (1) Turing/Volta mma fragment layout changes WHICH accumulator lane holds which softmax element - llama.cpp carries separate 'Turing + Volta' KQ_idx code (l % 2 vs l/2 % 2, and shuffle reduction offsets 2/1 vs Ampere) in fattn-mma; getting this wrong yields silently wrong attention, not a crash. (2) Online-softmax rescaling at DV=512/576 accumulates 512-dim PV products in half2 accumulators across nbatch_fa 32-row blocks with KQ_max per-thread replication across 4 threads on Turing - accumulation order differs from FlashMLA's fp32 Hopper path; the expf under-flow threshold (SOFTMAX_FTZ_THRESHOLD scaling trick) matters more as DV grows. (3) MLA absorbed decode must NOT apply RoPE to the 512 latent dims - only the 64-dim rope slice - and the weight-absorbed math (q_nope @ W_UK folded into V) is exactly what makes v_dim 512 != qk_dim 576; mixing absorbed and unabsorbed layouts (FlashMLA issue #49's exact confusion: 'head_size must be 576 while q_head_dim of DeepSeek-V3 is only 192') is the canonical correctness trap. (4) logit softcap path exists but sparse DSA gather forces nstages=1 and mask gathering per element - a wrong index fallback row (gather row 0 with -inf mask) silently perturbs outputs if indices are stale. No wrong-output bug reports specific to 576/512 on Turing were found; [uncertain] whether llama.cpp's Turing 576/512 path has production-hardened numerics at long context.
design_fit.demand_weighting: Weighting by deployed model mass over the tuple space: (576,512) has the largest absolute demand - DeepSeek-V3/R1/V3.2 plus Kimi-K2/K2.5/K3 (all DeepSeek-V3-architecture derivatives) dominate open-weight MoE serving, but nearly all of that demand is absorbed by Hopper/Blackwell owners running FlashMLA/FlashInfer; sm_75-relevant demand is the hobbyist/T4/2080Ti segment served almost exclusively by llama.cpp today (T4s remain the most common cheap cloud GPU). (256,256)+rope64 has fast-growing demand: GLM-5/5.2 (744B, promoted for 8xB200 and Ascend deployments) and Qwen3.5 (397B-A17B flagship plus smaller Qwen3.5 variants) both use it, and its d=256 core is directly in scope for the sm_75 bridge's ROUTE A. (192,128) is under-served everywhere: it is the prefill/naive MLA mode and MiMo-V2.5's shape, and llama.cpp is the only general kernel covering it. Kimi Linear-style hybrid fleets add per-layer dispatch overhead everywhere. Net: for an sm_75 bridge, prioritise (256,256,rope 64) and (192,128) (cheap, no competition), treat (576,512) as the high-visibility but llama.cpp-occupied niche, and rely on per-layer backend dispatch conventions (vLLM/SGLang HybridLinearAttnBackend pattern) so the bridge slots in as just another selectable MLA backend rather than replacing linear-attention paths.
